Two things you could try adding to your settings (`F1` > `Preferences: Open User Settings (JSON)`):

```json
  "github.copilot.advanced.debug.useElectronFetcher": false,
  "github.copilot.advanced.debug.useNodeFetcher": false,
  "github.copilot.advanced.debug.useNodeFetchFetcher": true
```

And if that doesn't work try:

```json
  "github.copilot.advanced.debug.useElectronFetcher": false,
  "github.copilot.advanced.debug.useNodeFetcher": true,
  "github.copilot.advanced.debug.useNodeFetchFetcher": false
```

Please let us know which of these doesn't work and which does!
I'm seeing this issue too starting today - none of the above suggestions are working.

FYI i at least managed to fix my issues - your initial suggestion failed UDP was probably correct, I was running a hyper-V VM at the same time as VS-Code which leverages a virtual network adapter to allow the VM to have an IP in my local network (i.e. not the default hyper-V switch). Within the VM I was using Citrix workspace, it seems that was the cause of the issue. If I use the VM but don't use Citrix workspace it works - anyway now I have just deleted the virtual adapter as I only needed it for SSH - now everything is working again, very odd issue though.

thanks for the first work for me

What finally resolved the issue for me was fixing one of my MCP tools. I had a custom MCP that worked with all agents except Google’s Gemini models. However, I encountered a warning: “failed validation: object has unsupported top-level schema keyword ‘oneOf’”. After modifying the MCP server code to eliminate the use of ‘oneOf’, the tool resumed functioning. Of course, disabling the MCP tool also worked as a solution. 

No more "Request Failed: 400 Bad Request" anymore

This issue has been closed as it has been labeled with `info-needed` and has not received the additional information that was requested from the issue author. It has been labeled as `info-needed` for 7 days.

comments.body: For me, the issue was resolved by disabling the Postman MCP server. Apparently, I don’t know why, but I had two MCP servers configured, which may have been conflicting with each other. As you can see below, there is a Postman server, and above it there is the Postman MCP server (which is the one I disabled). I tested them one by one, and when I disabled this one, the Gemini models started working correctly. My proposal to fix this issue would be to disable the MCP servers one by one, as shown above, and validate which one is causing the error.
